title: Beehive: A Flexible Network Stack for Direct-Attached Accelerators
problem: Modern datacenter network stacks are complex with interleaved protocol layers and virtualization support, while existing hardware network stacks only support basic protocols and use fixed processing pipelines that are difficult to extend.
motivation: Network feature agility, diagnostics, and manageability are critical for datacenter operators and must be matched with raw performance improvements.
method: Beehive is an FPGA-based network stack where application and network protocol elements are modularized as tiles over a network-on-chip substrate. Elements can be dynamically added or scaled to match workload characteristics with minimal changes to other components. The system provides flexible diagnostics and control mechanisms with tooling to ensure deadlock safety, and interoperates with standard Linux TCP and UDP clients.
key_novelty: Tile-based modular architecture over a network-on-chip substrate that enables flexible and adaptive construction of complex network functionality in hardware.
contributions: FPGA-based modular network stack with tile-based architecture over NoC substrate for direct-attached accelerators
Dynamic scaling and reconfiguration of network elements to adapt to workload characteristics
Integrated flexible diagnostics and control mechanisms with deadlock safety guarantees
4x improvement in end-to-end RPC tail latency compared to CPU-attached accelerators

metrics.speedup: 4x reduction in end-to-end RPC tail latency (Linux UDP clients vs CPU-attached accelerator)

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Flexible modular FPGA-based network stack for accelerators
